item.title: MKV QuickPlay 2.6.0
item.description:
MKV QuickPlay 2.6.0

Added

  • Shortcuts, Siri & Spotlight support. Seven actions — Preview Videos, Next/Previous Video, Move Current Video to Trash, Toggle Purple Tag, Stop Preview and Review Folder — now appear in the Shortcuts app and in Spotlight on macOS 26+, and all but Review Folder can be invoked by Siri ("Next video in MKV QuickPlay"). The Preview Videos action accepts files from other shortcuts or uses the current Finder selection when run bare.
  • Finder Quick Action. Build a one-action shortcut around Preview Videos and enable it as a Quick Action to get MKV QuickPlay in Finder's right-click Quick Actions menu — recipe in the README.
  • Watch folders. Point the app at your ingest folders (menu bar → Watch Folders → Add Folder…) and newly arrived videos are offered for review: a notification plus a count on the menu bar icon, one click to step through just the new files. Files still being copied are never offered — arrivals must settle first — and videos already in a folder when you add it don't count as new. Works across volume unmounts, remounts and sleep.

Fixed

  • Opening a video while the app wasn't running (double-click / Open With) crashed on launch; the files now open once the app finishes starting.
  • The keyboard shortcut silently did nothing on large Finder selections (a few hundred files or more). Reading the selection is now ~30× faster, handles 1000+ files in about a second, and explains itself if Finder ever fails to answer instead of staying silent.
  • Icon view folders sorted by Date or Size navigated in exactly the wrong direction (oldest/smallest first); they now match what Finder shows.
  • A trash keypress delivered during a session switch could act on the next session's video; stale player events are now discarded.
  • Trashing or undoing immediately after a preview opened could be undone by the background Finder-sort refresh (a trashed file reappearing in the playlist); the stale refresh is now discarded.
  • Previewing a hidden (dot-named) or symlinked video left the arrows dead and made Delete close the preview instead of advancing.
  • Alerts shown while a video was playing (About, How to Use, the shortcut recorder) swallowed every subsequent player key until the mpv window was clicked; key focus now returns to the player automatically.
  • Undoing a trash then pressing the shortcut again on the same selection wrongly closed the preview.
  • Holding the arrow keys through very long culling runs could exhaust file descriptors (stray cleanup watchdogs); file handles are now released immediately.
  • A filename containing a newline, or containing "-1743", could corrupt selection parsing or wrongly latch the "Automation denied" state.
  • Release tooling: a forgotten build-number bump used to publish an update Sparkle would never offer; the release scripts now refuse it, reject unknown flags, and verify the GitHub release exists before updating the Homebrew cask or appcast.

Full release on GitHub
